Ziggurat

A total rebalance of Age of Wonders

Ziggurat is a sister mod of AoWx, both enabled by AndG's AoW+ breakthroughs of 2020. Ziggurat's design leans more towards hard counters and experimental features than fine-tuned balance, though it is intended for PBEM play.

Unit Spellcasters

Units with the Spellcasting ability can now cast spells - although high-tier spells can now only be cast by high-tier Spellcasting ability - not by a tier2 Priest with Spellcasting I.

Racial Hero Levelups

Every ability has a chance to be available at each levelup, depending on the hero's race - heroes of different races will now have different capabilities no matter how much they level up.

5% hitchance increments

All ATK-DAM-DEF-RES-HP values in the game have been doubled, in order to allow for hitchance to increment by 5%, not 10%, per difference step. As seen in AoW2.

New Abilities

New abilities include Reforming Flesh, Drillmaster, Path of Sand, and the fourfold Evoker-Enchanter-Conjurer-Ritualist spellcasting discounts.

Reworked Abilities

Crossbowmen and Javelin-throwers exist, Cause Fear/Panic prevents launching melee attacks. Abilities such as Leadership, Marksmanship, and Vision have more levels than before. Spellcasting's mana generation partly depends on the Hero's RES attribute. And much more.

More dramatic counters

Charge is now +5 DAM on first hit, parry is +8 DEF, Invisibility grants +2 DEF in melee and +5 against ranged unless the attacker has True Seeing, Assassin grants +5/5 against heroes in melee and +2/2 at range, and so on!

Shipyards draw income from water area

Shipyards draw income from the size of the water body they're next to - divided between all shipyards on that water body.

Spell Reworks

Spell reworks include allowing Firestorm to turn Desert to Lava (not on unit-occupied hexes), and allowing Raise Terrain to block cave passages temporarily.

Gameplay diversity

More variety in abilities, spells and unit stats.

Theme

Graphical reworks in the style of the original game, new lore on unit cards, sound effects from Age of Mythology, and item sets cribbed from Dominions and Eador: Genesis.

Balance

Nerfs and buffs - but by weakening weak points and strengthening strong ones, so that counters, diversity and identity get exaggerated rather than flattened.

Most Radical Features

  • Units can cast spells - no longer heroes only.
  • New spells and new abilities, alongside brand-new and completely reworked units in every race.
  • Three reworked ranged abilities. Flame Throwing became Witchfire (lightning, poison and death damage - the Spider Queen and the Charlatan carry it). Shoot Black Javelin became Throw Javelin, a 4/4 attack for rank-and-file soldiers like the new Frostling Frakkaman and the Orc Javelineer, so not every race fields archers. Shoot Bolt arms ballistas, the new Dwarf Arbalester and the Human Crossbowman.

Less Radical Features

  • Units gain HP and MV from experience, even past gold medal - and every medal grants another point of ATK, RES, HP and MV, with DAM arriving at silver and DEF only at gold, so a veteran low-tier unit can trade with high-tier ones.
  • Summons are cheap to cast but expensive to keep. Raise a host when you need one; don't garrison with it.
  • Heroes no longer rush 10 DEF: DEF costs far more to level, while Spellcasting pays out much more in casting points and mana income.
  • Leadership runs to four levels, each granting every other unit in the party another point of both ATK and DEF - a leader gains nothing from its own level, only from the other leaders standing with it. Every leader has it, and so do units like the Firstborn and the Yaka Avatar.
  • Ranged attacks take -2 ATK underground unless the unit has Night Vision.
  • Vision is shorter all round, but concealment is far stronger - units hide beside any building bar guilds and shipyards, and in any trees, down to sparse scrub and giant toadstools. Every priest, cleric and shaman carries True Seeing to compensate.
  • Each race has its own abilities, generally at gold medal and built into its heroes. Orcs get Round Attack.
  • Race relations have far more wary and neutral pairings and far fewer polite or hostile ones. Dark Elves and Humans hate each other, as the lore demands.
  • Units inherit 50% of a unit's experience when they kill it.
  • Green and blue blood colours reimplemented - cut content from 1999.

Latest additions

  • Panic now breaks the moment anything lands a blow on the panicked unit - and a panicked unit can no longer start a melee fight, though it still retaliates.
  • Power Leech replaces Power Leak: it moves a quarter of every rival magic node's power to you instead of simply destroying it.
  • Maps can carry a Firmament above the surface - a fourth level of open Sky, reachable only by air.
  • Embrittle, a new Earth combat spell that doubles physical damage on its target, and Grip of Winter, which now cools the land through desert, steppe, grass and snow rather than only freezing water.
  • Astral Ward replaces Spell Ward, and blocks only Town Gate and Warp Party.
  • Items can carry hit points and movement, and the hero library's fifty heroes have had their skill points spent.

Thanks go to

  • And G, IniochReborn, Lagi, Thirsk and other older modders - for creating the modern hex-editing mod scene with AoW+, and for teaching us how to hex edit.
  • Codyksyp and IniochReborn - fellow disciples of And G, for their own mods Evolved and AoWx - we have all stolen ideas from each other.
  • Lagi - for the new unit graphics and several other graphical upgrades.
  • Thirsk and other older modders - whose unit graphics I may or may not have appropriated without checking exactly where they came from (sorry).
  • Lin Kuei Ominae - for a unit graphic - ppmforums.com/topic-44475

Major Changes

Units cast spells

Ordinary units can now cast spells, but the Spellcasting ability only generates mana on Heroes.

Razing, rebellion and looting are real battles

Razing structures, looting cities and city rebellion in general now trigger pre-emptive battles against raze defenders.

The Arena fights

The Arena is now a place for fighting battles in exchange for gold, XP and item rewards.

Combat log

The game now has a combat log.

Three medal ranks

Units now have three medals - Copper, Silver, Gold.

Whole-tier research

Instead of individual spell research, spells are now researched as tiers within a given sphere.

Sky and Chasm

Two new terrains - Sky above ground, Chasm below - passable only to flying and floating units.

A fourth map level

Maps can carry a Firmament above the surface, filled with Sky and reachable only by air. See New Mechanics.

Hero level-up, reorganised

Hero levelup dialog is far bigger, with most abilities available, split into five columns.

Use items work

Use items grant their listed stats, immunities, protections and abilities while carried.

New Mechanics

Five-percent steps and doubled stats

  • One point of ATK over the target's DEF is worth 5 percentage points of hit chance, where vanilla paid 10. Equal stats still hit half the time, and the roll is still held between 10% and 90%.
  • Every ATK, DEF, RES, DAM and HP number in the game was doubled to pay for it. At the same matchup the hit chance and the whole damage spread are exactly what they were - the point of the change is that half-steps now exist. A modifier can be worth 5 percentage points where the smallest step used to be 10.
  • The limits sit where they always did: +8 ATK over DEF hits 90%, -8 hits 10%. Odd differences fill in between - +1 is 55%, +3 is 65%, and so on.
  • Not everything doubled, and what did not is now half as strong. Item bonuses are still +1 to +3, and the ATK, DEF and RES a medal grants are unchanged. Movement, status durations and the flat percentage chances were left alone deliberately.
  • Buffs and debuffs sit one notch below the doubled value, spending the odd grades the change opened up - Stone Skin is +3 DEF rather than +4, Poisoned is -3/-3 rather than -4/-4.
  • Ceilings. Units stop at 40 ATK and 60 DEF, RES and DAM; heroes stop at 40 on all four. Both cap at 100 HP. Debuffs can drive ATK, DEF and RES all the way to 0; a hero's DAM and HP will not go below 2.
  • Hero stat prices were halved so the sums still work: 3 skill points per point of ATK, 6 per DEF, 2 per RES, 4 per DAM, 2 per HP, and Movement unchanged at 3. What a hero can buy now stops exactly where the game stops reading it - points spent above the ceiling used to vanish.
  • The 10% auto-miss and 10% auto-max are untouched. Two faces of the die in twenty always miss and two always deal the attack's full damage rating, whatever the stats. At -8 or worse the auto-max band is the only way to connect, so such an attacker lands one blow in ten and every one of them lands full. Being 8 down and being 40 down are the same thing.
  • Excess ATK buys minimum damage. Past +8 the hit chance is pinned and the surplus starts cutting off the low damage rolls instead: against a damage rating of 10, +12 guarantees at least 3 and +20 at least 5. It is worth little on light hitters and a great deal on heavy ones, and it is why sieges feel so much steadier than field battles - walls have next to no Defence, so the whole of the attacker's ATK counts as the difference.
  • Morale went back on the doubled scale, and it now moves Attack too: -4 / -2 / 0 / +2 / +4 by band, against -6 / -4 / -2 / 0 / +2 on Resistance, for units and heroes alike. Defence is out of it altogether. Vanilla moved Defence and Resistance and had no Attack link at all, so morale now works on the opposite pair from the one you may remember.
  • Walls were unified at 40 hit points for stone and 10 for wood, city doors counting as wood. The game keeps three separate wall tables - one for the pre-battle prediction, one for auto-resolve and one for the battle you fight by hand - and they had drifted apart, so the same wall could be worth 13, 20 or 48 depending on how the fight got resolved. Vanilla was 10 and 5, so this is a balance decision rather than part of the doubling.
  • The odds are not guesswork: the combat log prints the hit percentage together with the ATK and DEF it came from.
  • Saves made before the rescale cannot be carried over. Heroes load light on every stat, roughly half the skill points they spent come back, and current HP reads halved. Start a new game.

Vision blocked by Earth and Rock

  • Earth and Rock block line of sight. A hex is revealed only if a clear line runs to it; a wall of Earth or Rock in the way leaves everything behind it dark. Vanilla revealed every hex inside the radius whatever stood in between.
  • You always see the near face of a wall. The blocking hex itself stays visible; what is behind it, deeper wall hexes included, does not. Neighbouring hexes are always visible, since nothing can stand between.
  • Nothing sees past it. Vision level, Flying, Night Vision and True Seeing make no difference - this is terrain against terrain. Only Earth and Rock block: Mountains, Forest and Hills sit on top of the terrain rather than being it, and do not.
  • Where two equally short lines reach a hex, either one being clear is enough, so a wall never blanks out a hex you can plainly see around.
  • Mapping is blocked as well as sight. You do not chart the ground behind a wall, and that includes the two extra rings of terrain-only vision beyond your sight range.
  • It applies to everything that sees on your behalf - armies, cities, towers, Watchers, Reflecting Pools, and your allies' units. Bird's View now reveals a line-of-sight shape rather than a clean disc.
  • Earth can be opened; Rock cannot. Level Terrain turns an Earth wall into dirt, and nothing removes Rock at all. A sight line opened mid-turn lights up at the start of your next turn rather than the instant the ground changes.
  • In practice this is an underground rule. Earth and Rock are what the caves are cut out of, so the world below now reads as corridors and chambers instead of a lit disc around each stack.
  • The AI is not blinded by it - it still acts on units and hexes that have gone dark to you.

The Firmament

  • A map can carry a fourth level above the surface, the Firmament. The World Map strip reads Firmament, Surface, Caverns, Depths from left to right, and Page Up and Page Down walk it in that order. A map built with the usual three levels is untouched and shows three tabs as it always did.
  • The Firmament is Sky, edge to edge - the same terrain that can appear in patches on the surface. Only flying and floating units can enter it, and bridges cross it. Everything else has no way up there at all.
  • Sight works as it does on the surface, not as it does underground: no Earth or Rock to block a line, and the same two extra rings of terrain-only vision.
  • Map-wide and targeted map spells reach it, storms included, and Bird's View reveals it like any other level.
  • Air elementals heal on it, earth elementals do not. The Firmament is air, so it counts as their element for the per-hex elemental heal and not as anybody else's.
  • The level is called the Firmament; the terrain that fills it is still called Sky.

Items that grant hit points and movement

  • Items can carry hit points and movement. Thirty-two of them do: up to +12 HP on the life-themed armour and rings, and up to +6 MV on the boots and wind items. Vanilla items could grant neither.
  • The bonus can be negative. A cursed item is free to take hit points or movement away, and the arithmetic handles it.
  • Worn items always count; a spare in the backpack does not. The exception is a use item, which grants what it carries from the backpack as well - the same rule use items already follow for their stats and abilities.
  • It reaches the hero's card, tactical combat and auto-resolve alike, and it is applied before the hero's own ceiling rather than after it, so an item cannot push a hero past 100 HP or 80 MV.
  • Heroes and leaders only. An item lying on the map or held in the library grants nothing.

Shipyards and water income

  • A shipyard earns 1 gold a turn for every 5 hexes of the water it adjoins. Vanilla shipyards earned nothing at all - they were pure ship production, and that part is unchanged.
  • The gold from one body of water is split evenly between every finished shipyard on it, whoever owns them. Two shipyards on a 200-hex sea show 20 each, not 40.
  • An independent shipyard takes its share and keeps nothing. A derelict on your sea is a standing tax until you raze it or take it.
  • Razed and half-built shipyards neither earn nor count towards the split. Finishing one, or razing one, moves everybody's share that same turn.
  • A shipyard between two seas draws a divided share from each - a share of both, not the larger of the two, and not the sum of their areas.
  • Water bodies never span map levels. An underground sea is never part of the surface sea above it.
  • Ice is not water. Freezing a strait shrinks a body or cuts it in two and takes the income with it, though ice from Grip of Winter melts back after a few turns. Flood makes new water and merges bodies, and takes it away again when it lapses. A bridge over water changes nothing - the hex still counts.
  • Fractions are lost twice, once at the count and once at the split. A pond of fewer than 5 hexes pays nothing, and a shipyard earning nothing shows no income line at all.
  • The water is recounted once a day, so a terrain change reaches the income at the next turn rather than the moment it happens.
  • The gold appears on the shipyard's own panel and as a Shipyards row in the Realm window. It does not drop while the shipyard is building a ship.
  • A shipyard costs 20 gold to build against vanilla's 50, and 10 gold and one turn to repair against 25 gold and two.

Astral Ward

  • Spell Ward is renamed Astral Ward.
  • Astral Ward blocks Town Gate and Warp Party, and nothing else. Vanilla's Spell Ward blocked every strategic-map spell in the game while it stood.
  • It blocks every player, not just its owner's rivals. One ward anywhere on the map stops both spells for everybody, the caster included.
  • Global enchantments are unaffected. Hatred, the Masteries, Enchanted Roads, Power Leech and the rest cast and run normally under a ward.
  • Summons, storms, city spells and unit enchantments are unaffected.
  • Disjunction works normally under a ward, on enemy global enchantments and on the Astral Ward itself.
  • A ward stops the two spells from the moment it is up until it is dispelled or expires; both are castable again the same turn it goes.

Power Leech

  • Power Leak is renamed Power Leech, and no longer halves anybody's power.
  • The caster takes 25% of the power of every magic node held by another player. A node yields 12 power, so each one leeched moves 3 power a turn.
  • The owner loses exactly what the caster gains. Nothing is created and nothing is destroyed.
  • Only nodes another player owns are leeched. An unclaimed node gives nothing, and the caster's own nodes are left alone.
  • Cities, hero mana generation and every other power source are untouched. Magic nodes only.
  • A razed node, or one with a building on it, yields nothing to leech, exactly as it yields nothing to its owner.
  • Only one Power Leech may be active on the map at a time, cast by anybody. That was already true of Power Leak.
  • The transfer starts the turn the spell lands and stops the turn it is dispelled or its caster is defeated. It follows nodes as they change hands.
  • The leeched power reaches mana income and research allocation together, in the same proportion the caster has set.
  • The Magic window's power list carries the transfer as its own row. The caster sees Power Leech (gained) with a positive value; every player losing power sees Power Leech (lost) with a negative one. Power Base above the list stays the raw, un-leeched total.

New Abilities

New abilities (10)

  • Path of Sand - leaves desert in the unit's wake.
  • Magebane - +1/1 ATK/DAM against enchanted targets, stacking with the number of enchantments on them.
  • Drillmaster - every other unit in the stack gains +1 XP per turn, stacking per Drillmaster. Other Drillmasters and heroes are excluded.
  • Assassin - +3 ATK / +3 DAM in melee against heroes.
  • Shield - ranged only. Shots and breath attacks that land on the unit are made at -5 ATK, which is 25 percentage points off the attacker's chance to hit. In a battle you fight by hand it covers fire arriving from the hex in front of the unit or one hex to the side of that; an auto-resolved battle has no facings, so there it applies to three shots in four instead. The roll is per shot, so a three-shot archer is blunted on about two of the three. Melee is Parry's job - that takes 8 off the first melee blow from any direction - and the two are bought separately. No unit carries Shield as standard.
  • Evoker - halves the mana cost of the 30 spells that exist only as combat spells.
  • Conjurer - halves the mana cost of the 13 summoning spells.
  • Enchanter - halves the mana cost of the 18 spells cast on a single unit, whether yours or an enemy's.
  • Ritualist - halves the mana cost of the 12 global enchantments.
  • The four casting discounts cover 73 of the 108 spells between them; storms, terrain spells, city spells, hero spells and targeted map spells get no discount from any of them. All four are bought once, in the Magic column at level-up. A hero can hold several, but no spell belongs to two families, so they never stack.

Reworked abilities (10)

  • Slayer abilities reach ranged combat - Assassin, Monster Slaying, Holy Champion and Unholy Champion add +1 ATK / +1 DAM on shots and breath attacks against their target type, stacking.
  • Leadership I-IV - four levels at 10 skill points each, granting every other unit in the party +1/+1, +2/+2, +3/+3 and +4/+4 ATK/DEF. Vanilla had a single level worth +1/+1. Leadership was deliberately left off the doubled scale, so level II is worth what vanilla's one level was and level I is a step down from it.
  • Leadership never buffs its own holder - the bonus a unit gets is the best Leadership level among the others in its party. Two leaders in one stack buff each other; a leader travelling alone with ordinary troops gains nothing itself. The card shows both halves, e.g. “Leadership III (+IV received)”.
  • Leadership IV makes the whole stack Fearless - nothing in it can be panicked, by Terror or by a Cause Fear blow, in a battle you fight by hand or an auto-resolved one. The hero granting it is covered too. Immunity is fixed when the battle starts, so it holds for the rest of the fight even if that hero dies.
  • Turn Undead - damage scales with the caster's Resistance (½ × level × RES, rounded); the ability card shows the real number.
  • Life Stealing and Dark Gift - the heal now also triggers on Round Attack hits (offensive melee only, never retaliation or ranged).
  • Path of Life / Decay / Frost - radius 2: the inner ring always converts the ground, the new outer ring at 25%.
  • Fire heals Fire units - Firestorm, burning hexes and Fire Barrier heal Fire Elementals and Fire Sprites, with a +N popup.
  • Invisibility - grants +1 DEF in melee and +3 DEF against ranged attacks unless the attacker has True Seeing.
  • Night Vision - ranged attacks made underground suffer -2 ATK unless the attacker has Night Vision.

Casting with units

  • Any unit with the Spellcasting ability casts from your researched spellbook - so research something castable before expecting it to do anything.
  • It spends casting points, refilled every turn by Spellcasting level: 10 / 20 / 40 / 60 / 90 for I to V.
  • A spell costing no more than the unit's points is cast instantly; a dearer one is channelled over as many turns as it takes.
  • The mana comes from your pool. Units never generate mana - only heroes do, at Resistance x Spellcasting level per turn.
  • An ordinary unit needs Spellcasting level at least equal to the spell's tier. Spells above its level are hidden from its book rather than offered and refused. Heroes and your leader are exempt - a hero casts anything in your spellbook at any Spellcasting level, and pays only the mana and the casting points.
  • Cosmos spells stay exclusive to heroes and your leader - they never appear in an ordinary unit's book.
  • Casting points are shown on the unit card, and a part-channelled spell survives save and load.
  • Works in auto-resolve, in tactical combat and on the strategic map.

Behaviour changes

  • Ice Storm turns lava into wasteland instead of snow.
  • Raise Terrain cast on lava dries each hex at 50% into dirt instead of raising mountains.
  • Raise Terrain can be cast underground, where it seals dirt into a wall of Earth for two to four of your turns before it collapses back to dirt. Vanilla refused the cast below the surface outright. With sight now blocked by Earth, this closes a corridor as well as a road. Its surface behaviour is unchanged.
  • Freeze Water became Grip of Winter, and it now cools the land as well as freezing water. Cast on any explored hex with no army and no structure on it, the target hex and its six neighbours each step one place along desert to steppe to grass to snow, and stop at snow. Water still turns to ice as before. One step per cast, so desert takes three casts to reach snow, and the cooling melts back the same way the ice always has. Wasteland, lava, dirt and ice are not on the ladder.
  • Terror is effectively once per battle, per side. After a side lands it, that side will not reach for it again unless Terror is the only combat spell it owns. In an auto-resolved battle the cap is absolute and applies to you as well, so auto-resolving costs you Terror casts you would have had fighting the battle yourself. Each side has its own allowance and every new battle resets both.
  • Animate Dead raises permanent undead. What it summons survives the battle and joins your army as an ordinary unit - no upkeep, no mana, and no enchantment to dispel. Which undead you get varies. Recall Spirit is unchanged and its spirits still vanish when the fight ends.
  • Crusade raises one of three warbands - an Astra-led tier-1 host, Valkyries with a tier-2 mix, or three mixed stacks with a catapult - instead of the same units every time.
  • Sphere Mastery re-prices casting: opposed spheres ×1.5 (was ×2) and your own sphere ×0.75. It is a global enchantment, so it re-prices that sphere for every wizard in the game, not only the one who cast it.
  • No spell costs less than 1 mana. A discount can no longer drive a cast down to nothing, which used to consume neither mana nor a casting point. A spell whose base cost is genuinely zero still costs zero.
  • Sphere Mastery now reaches instantly-cast summons and global enchantments. They used to re-read the undiscounted price and escape the multiplier altogether, so they were neither cheaper on your own sphere nor dearer on an opposed one.

New Spells

New spells (1)

SpellSphereTierManaUpkeepResearch
EmbrittleEarthTier 314-80

What they do

  • Embrittle is cast in a battle you fight by hand, at one enemy unit, and is resisted the same way Slow is. If it lands, that unit is Embrittled for the rest of the battle and every hit on it that carries physical damage does double. It is the exact mirror of Physical Protection: against a unit that has both, the two cancel and damage comes out normal. Against Physical Immunity it does nothing at all, and the cast is still spent.

Picking spheres. Water/Fire and Earth/Air sphere pairs can now be combined up to a total of 4 spheres within each pair, so 1/3, 2/2 and 0/4 are pickable. Death and Life are still totally incompatible.All three pairs of opposition spheres completely incompatible.

Research

  • You research a whole tier of a sphere at once, not one spell at a time. A single entry such as Fire II grants every spell of that sphere and tier together.
  • Tier cost is flat - 100, 200, 400 and 800 research points for tiers I to IV, regardless of which sphere or how many spells the tier holds.
  • You start knowing a complete tier-1 sphere, drawn at random from the spheres your leader picked (Cosmos only if you picked nothing else).
  • The research entry lists the spells the tier will grant, so you can see what you are buying before you commit.

Experience needed for each medal.

  • Ziggurat adds a third rank. The ladder is None → Copper → Silver → Gold, where the old one ran straight from None to Silver to Gold.
  • Bonuses are cumulative - each rank grants another point of ATK, RES, HP and MV, so the medals are a steady climb rather than one jump at the top. Damage arrives at silver and Defence at gold.
  • Thresholds scale with unit tier, so a tier-1 unit reaches copper at 2 XP while a tier-4 unit needs 8. Cheap units decorate quickly.
  • Movement from experience was slowed to +1 MV per 4/6/8/10 XP by unit level, from the previous 2/4/6/8, so medals now carry more of the movement growth than XP does. HP from experience is unchanged at +1 per 2/3/4/5.
  • Warmonger now grants a flat 15 XP, making it powerful for low-level units specifically.
  • Drillmaster grants all units in a stack +1 XP per turn.

The hero library

  • The fifty heroes you can recruit arrive with their skill points already spent. They had been carrying them unspent - 589 points between them, one hero holding 26 - which showed up as a nag on the recruitment screen and as stats well below what the hero's level claimed.
  • Where a hero was holding more than a level's worth, its level came down to match what it had actually bought. Seven dropped two levels. The points themselves went into hit points and attack.
  • Three heroes still show exactly one unspent point, which is not enough to buy anything.

Hero chassis

Every hero is built on a chassis - a per-race statline that its own level-up points, items, morale and abilities then build on. There are three per race: the mounted Hero, the slower and frailer Infantry hero, and the Leader you play. Ability bonuses are not counted here - a Leadership bonus received from another leader in the same stack is on top. A hero's own Leadership adds nothing to itself.

Min stats (after debuffs)01Attack, Defence and Resistance can be driven all the way to 0. A hero's Damage and hit points stop at 2.

Changed in Ziggurat

  • Storm debuffs can be resisted - Pestilence, Death Storm and Divine Storm debuffs are rolled against Resistance instead of landing automatically, and a matching Protection adds +2 to the roll. Machines cannot get Vertigo.
  • Webbed and Entangled work on units - the penalty now applies to ordinary units; vanilla only ever applied it to heroes.
  • A panicked unit cannot start a melee fight, exactly as a walker cannot swing at a flyer overhead: it will not attack, take a free swing or use a touch ability against an enemy. It still retaliates at full strength when something attacks it, and friendly touch abilities are unaffected, so a panicked healer still heals. A panicked archer still shoots.
  • Any blow that lands snaps a unit out of Panic - melee, shot, breath, spell, touch, a burning or decay tick, in a battle you fight or one you auto-resolve. A miss does not, and neither does a hit fully absorbed to nothing. This matters more than it sounds: Panic has no timer, so before this the only ways out of it were Healing, Remedy, or the end of the battle.

Bugfixes

Game

  • Cursor dead zone on small maps - on a small map in a wide window, the right and bottom of the map ignored the mouse - the cursor froze and clicks did nothing over real hexes.
  • Leadership could be lost for ever - a unit that earned Leadership while inside another leader's aura never received its own copy, and lost Leadership permanently once the aura left. The grant now checks the unit's own level, so an aura cannot mask it.
  • Webbed and Entangled do their job - both showed their icon and ticked down, but the -2 DEF never applied to ordinary units (heroes were fine). The penalty now lands the moment the effect does.
  • Mixed stacks move their full distance - a stack with mixed movement types predicted and walked a shorter path than it could really make - the slowest unit's points were priced at the worst mover's costs. Prediction, arrows and the executed move now use each unit's true reach.
  • A single Great Eagle could raze an entire city - the strength check simulates a battle, and melee defenders who cannot reach a flyer were dropped from it entirely instead of soaking blows and retaliating - so one eagle killed the archers, won outright, and could raze anything up to a metropolis. The check now charges melee retaliation, and four eagles cannot reliably repress a three-hex city.
  • The AI considers razing everything it captures - vanilla only asked “should I raze this?” after a battle - anything captured by walking in was never evaluated.
  • Item-granted Healing is once per turn - Healing or Dispel Magic from an item could be used every round, for ever: the once-per-turn flag was written to the hero but read back from the item.
  • Marksmanship on items works - an item carrying Marksmanship added nothing, even on slots the game itself allows it on - the ranged-attack code never looked at items.
  • Leadership aura applies at once - buying a Leadership level left the stack without the stronger aura until the army next moved. It refreshes on the spot.
  • Exploration sites roll their own defenders - every site of the same type and strength spawned the identical defender set all match, and dungeons the same prisoners - the generator never advanced the dice. Each site now rolls its own.
  • Slippery Bridge bug - fixed.

Known issues

  • Boarding transports can, rarely, swallow a unit - a rare vanilla defect can make a unit - most often a lone hero - vanish when boarding a transport. Analysed, not yet fixed. If a transport starts refusing or losing passengers, stop using it.

Editor

AoWDevEd improvements

  • Random Party generator - the Party tool opens a dialog (strength, behaviour, eligible races) and places a randomly generated stack. Untick every race for the vanilla empty party.
  • Map Validation is clickable - double-click an entry to jump straight to the offending object, switching level if needed.
  • Terrain palette - Sky and Chasm brushes, plus cross-level painting: surface terrains on the Underground tab and vice versa.
  • Four Rank Abilities tabs - the unit editor edits base, Copper, Silver and Gold ability sets separately.
  • Use-item stat spinners un-greyed - use items can carry authored stats.
  • File dialogs remember their folders - map, set and text dialogs each keep their own last directory, across sessions.
  • No more 15 fps editor - the map view no longer paces the whole editor; object placement and palette switching are immediate, idle CPU is down from ~29% to ~5%, and input latency roughly halved.
  • Menu toolbar and start-maximised - the menu bar carries a captioned toolbar row and the editor opens maximised.
  • The toolbar is one row, and every button is labelled - File: New, Open, Save, Save As; Developer: Open Mapset, Fog of War; Help: About. Twenty-four unlabelled buttons and the second row are gone, and the map view starts 31 pixels higher for it.
  • File > New offers a generated map - the Ziggurat map generator behind a panel of dials. A slider sets how much of the map is sea; graded dials cover sea ice, rivers, lakes, relief, erosion, structure, rain shadow, valley cutting, river greening, mountains, hills and islands, and a separate control picks which edge is cold. It lays down terrain, gives water a shallow shore, runs mountains as ranges rather than blobs, and places hills.
  • Developer > Delete Unused Heroes - prunes the open map's hero roster to the heroes actually placed on it plus the leaders, and tells you how many it will remove before it does. Placement counts wherever it is: a tile army, a city garrison or a site's defenders.
  • The mouse wheel scrolls the editor's own scrollbars, which ignored it before.
  • Level Up and Level Down follow the Firmament order on a four-level map, matching the game's own strip rather than the raw level numbers.
